message.content:
Let \(p\) be the probability of rolling face \(F\), and let \(q\) be the probability of rolling the face opposite \(F\). The other four faces each have probability \(1/6\).

Since the total probability is \(1\),

\[
p+q+4\cdot \frac16=1
\]

so

\[
p+q=\frac13.
\]

For two rolls, the probability of obtaining a sum of \(7\) comes from opposite-face pairs. The pair \((F,7-F)\) contributes \(pq\). Each of the other two opposite pairs contributes

\[
\frac16\cdot \frac16=\frac1{36}.
\]

Thus

\[
P(\text{sum}=7)=2\left(pq+2\cdot \frac1{36}\right)
=2pq+\frac19.
\]

We are given

\[
2pq+\frac19=\frac{47}{288}.
\]

So

\[
2pq=\frac{47}{288}-\frac{32}{288}=\frac{15}{288}=\frac{5}{96},
\]

and therefore

\[
pq=\frac{5}{192}.
\]

Now \(p\) and \(q\) satisfy

\[
p+q=\frac13,\qquad pq=\frac{5}{192}.
\]

The quadratic with roots \(p,q\) is

\[
t^2-\frac13t+\frac{5}{192}=0.
\]

Its discriminant is

\[
\left(\frac13\right)^2-4\cdot \frac{5}{192}
=\frac19-\frac{5}{48}
=\frac{1}{144}.
\]

So

\[
p,q=\frac{\frac13\pm \frac1{12}}{2}.
\]

This gives

\[
p=\frac{5}{24},\qquad q=\frac18.
\]

Since \(p>1/6\), we take

\[
p=\frac{5}{24}.
\]

Thus \(m=5\), \(n=24\), and

\[
m+n=29.
\]

The answer is 29.
